newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma jails 14 for involvement in student protests.
newsitem.headline: Burma jails 14 for involvement in student protests.

text.p: Burma said on Tuesday that 14 people, including five members of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's political party, had each been jailed for seven years for involvement in last month's student unrest.

The military government said in a statement that the five members of the National League for Democracy (NLD) and nine others were found guilty of agitation and throwing rocks at security personnel during the unrest.
A spokesman for the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) said they were now in Rangoon's Insein jail and were sentenced by the court on Monday.
"None of those sentenced were students," the statement said.

Thousands of Rangoon university students launched anti-government street protests in the capital in December to seek greater freedoms. More than 800 students were briefly detained for taking part in the protests.
The protests were the biggest in the capital since the pro-democracy uprising of 1988, which was crushed by the military and left thousands dead or in jail.
The SLORC shut down universities in the capital indefinitely and sent students home to the provinces. The universities are still closed.
Suu Kyi had maintained that her NLD party was not involved in the student unrest. But she said that she supported the students' demands for greater freedom in the country.
